mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when this trigger is met, contradicting the predicted negative direction.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which boosts wage growth and corporate pricing power, driving higher earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not statistically greater than zero (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when this trigger is active.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) for two consecutive quarters signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the correlation between GDPC1 decline and SPX returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% signals contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during months with INDPRO declines exceeding -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent fall in both personal savings (RSAFS) and consumer spending (GDPC1) signals a drawdown in household financial buffers and reduced consumption, which depresses corporate sales and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and GDPC1 both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of co-down months for RSAFS and GDPC1, or the joint signal does not outperform a single-proxy trigger in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is cut by at least 0.5% in a single FOMC meeting, liquidity conditions ease, lowering risk premia and boosting equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.10) following FEDFUNDS cuts of 0.5% or more.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the unemployment rate and a fall in payroll employment (UNRATE up and PAYEMS down) signals a sharp labor market deterioration, which reduces corporate profit margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases and PAYEMS decreases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls in the same month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) below 1,500 thousand units for three consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which drags on construction and materials sectors and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when HOUST remains below 1,500 for three straight months (t-test p > 0.05).
